v1_port.features: the preregistered v1_state block, asserted equal at build time
v1_port.verdict: POOLED WEEKS: passes. Lower Brier than both internal baselines, paired CI excludes zero, calibration slope 0.956 and intercept -0.034 inside the registered gates, and no single season contributes more than 16.7% of the gain.

week1_finding.also_rejected: a Week-1-only training set — worse on every arm
week1_finding.cause: EWMA form carries last season's scoring into an opener played by a substantially different team — precisely what week_one_policy warned against
week1_finding.explicitly_not_claimed: the week-1 arm is NOT a demonstrated improvement over plain causal Elo: paired by season the mean Brier difference is -0.00224 with a 95% interval [-0.00503,+0.00099], which INCLUDES ZERO

full_v1_arm_week1.verdict: FAILS the registered calibration gates on Week 1 and does not beat plain Elo

week1_finding.headline: the validated pooled result does NOT carry to season openers

what_this_unblocks: not v2. It unblocks the preregistration's own week_one_policy, which says that when the Week 1 blocks are missing the system publishes v1 baseline forecasts with V2_INPUT_BLOCKED — and that requires a clean v1 port, which was recorded ABSENT_AT_PREREGISTRATION and now exists.
why_not_further: RUNNING, not ACQUIRED. Schedules for 2001-2025 are bound with per-file hashes, but v2's ordered feature blocks also require play-by-play EPA, success rate, explosiveness, talent, returning production, quarterback and coach continuity. NONE of those were acquired. Moving to DATA_ACQUIRED_FEATURE_BUILD_PENDING would assert a completeness that does not exist.
